question: What does the fixed stopping rule actually predict before any language, physical carrier or context learner is supplied?
premises: A fixed non-erasing one-source-letter/one-skeleton-unit projection pi.
Fixed left-to-right order of ambiguous source positions.
An explicit independently licensed candidate set D, with intended spelling w in D for the ordinary branch.
Complete literal fallback if w is outside D; no physical rendering has been fixed.

deductions.claim: In the ordinary branch all supplement payloads for the same w are prefixes of one fixed source-letter sequence, even for non-nested candidate sets.
deductions.proof: Let ambiguous positions be i1,...,im and S(w)=w[i1]...w[im]. Candidate sets change only the stopping index k. Every supplement is S(w)[:k], so any two payloads are prefix-comparable. No nesting assumption is needed for comparability.

deductions.claim: If w belongs to D2 subset D1, the stop index for D2 cannot exceed that for D1.
deductions.proof: At each index k the surviving D2 set is a subset of surviving D1 and contains w. As soon as D1 becomes {w}, D2 must also be {w}. It may have become singleton earlier.

deductions.claim: The ordinary branch is not character deletion: its skeleton has length n and its raw letter-unit payload has length n+k.
deductions.proof: Each of n source letters emits exactly one skeleton unit, then k literal supplement letters are added. This is an abstract unit count, not a bound on ink, physical glyphs or comparison with another encoding.

deductions.claim: At most m+1 ordinary supplement alternatives exist for one spelling, plus its literal fallback if that is available.
deductions.proof: k is an integer from0 throughm. This is not the at-most-two-alias premise of1226 for general words.

hand_example.purpose: All ordinary supplements form one prefix chain, including first and third non-nested candidate sets. No real language or native value is assigned.

scope_corrections: The previous user-facing phrase shortened words was inaccurate for this non-erasing skeleton module.

Prefix-chain consequence applies to abstract supplement payloads in the ordinary branch. It does not unconditionally apply to complete physical surface strings: delimiters, unbound carrier and the full-literal fallback remain separate.
Different native forms cannot be declared variants of the same source spelling merely because they resemble one another. No such binding is made here.
The added-supplement count is not physical glyph length until a complete carrier is specified.

A publicly computable context rule can be jointly hypothesized and tested; independent confirmation of word meanings is not a prerequisite for all exploration. But no actual such rule is supplied by971.
